messages:
Jin: heads-up: seeing a sustained shift in token mix this week — a lot more long-context streaming sessions from eu-west. avg tokens/session jumped ~1.2k -> ~4.5k over 72h :chart_with_upwards_trend:
ops-bot: [autoscale] sustained queue > 120 for model rwd-13b-quant in eu-west-1 (5m window) :warning:
Sanjay: can you drop the rough numbers? how many GPU hours are we looking at if this holds?
Jin: quick calc: baseline month = 18,000 GPU-hrs. with current token mix + 15% user growth projection ≈ 27,500 GPU-hrs (+~53%). streaming vs non-streaming mix reduces effective throughput/GPU by ~30% due to kv/cache churn and per-token IO.
Lucy: oof. cost impact estimate?
Maureen: rough ballpark: if we absorb in reserved pools (internal cost ≈ $1.8/GPU-hr) extra = ~$16k/mo. on-demand pricing (~$3.2/GPU-hr) -> extra ~$45k/mo.
Hiro: regional squeeze: eu-west reserved usage at ~92% this week. shifting capacity from hosted eu-west is non-trivial. us-west has spare capacity but p99 latency will increase ~20-35ms for EU clients.
Jin: options: 1) temporarily scale dedicated pool in us-west and route some traffic (accept p99 bump), 2) enable more aggressive batching + KV prefix caching for streaming, 3) pre-warm spot pools overnight for peak windows, 4) short-term throttling for low-priority/non-prod routes.
Sanjay: we need a throughput model that accounts for streaming overhead. quick sim config below (canary):
```
autoscale:
  target_inflight: 200
  scale_up: >80% gpu_util for 2m
  scale_down: <40% for 5m
batching:
  max_batch_tokens: 8192
  prefer_streaming_batch_size: 4
kv_cache:
  ttl_seconds: 86400  # 24h
```
Lucy: if we batch more we risk tail latency. need route-level SLO evals before pushing aggressive batching. also could nudge clients to early summarization or chunking to reduce avg context.
Maureen: I'll notify sales/support for customers in eu-west about potential latency/cost impacts and ask them to flag critical workloads. also pausing non-prod heavy jobs might buy us a week.
Hiro: i'll run a 72h capacity sim with current hour-by-hour traffic and the new token distribution, post results by EOD. cc @Sanjay for cost numbers.
Sanjay: thanks. low-effort win: enable kv-cache TTL=24h for repeated prefixes — our evals show ~8% compute reduction on streaming-heavy workloads. worth toggling on canary.
Jin: agreed. checklist: 1) run sim (Hiro), 2) enable kv-ttl on canary (ops), 3) test batch tuning on 10% canary route, 4) update routing policy to prefer us-west for new sessions if p99 delta acceptable, 5) sales advisory (Maureen). reconvene 10:30 UTC tomorrow to decide scale-up. :thumbsup:
